kept.excerpt: Russian forces continued offensive operations in the Hulyaipole direction and in western Zaporizhia Oblast on July 17 and 18 but did not advance.
kept.publisher: Institute for the Study of War
kept.relevance: The resolution-source institution’s cutoff-day assessment provides the latest verified sector-level evidence for the area around Ternuvate, although it does not establish the settlement’s precise map shading.

kept.excerpt: Russian forces continued offensive operations in the Hulyaipole direction and western Zaporizhia Oblast on July 16 and 17 but did not advance. Neither Ukrainian nor Russian forces made confirmed advances on July 17.
kept.publisher: Institute for the Study of War
kept.relevance: The preceding daily assessment helps establish recent battlefield momentum in Ternuvate’s sector before the forecasting cutoff.

kept.excerpt: A Ukrainian regiment operating in the Oleksandrivka direction announced on July 13 that Ukrainian forces liberated Ternove, Zaporizke, Novoheorhiivka, Vorone, Sichneve, and Maliivka, liberating 120 square kilometers and advancing 25 kilometers in depth. The regiment seemingly deleted its original announcement without issuing a formal statement retracting its initial report later on July 13. Ukrainian forces began counterattacks in the Oleksandrivka direction in Winter 2026, liberating around 480 square kilometers in Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhia oblasts since January 2026.
kept.relevance: This assessment documents Ukrainian counterattack pressure in the neighboring operational area while preserving the uncertainty surrounding the regiment’s announcement; Ternove is a different settlement from Ternuvate.

kept.excerpt: RM’s analysis of ISW data indicates that in the past four weeks (June 16–July 14, 2026), Russia made a net gain of 5 square miles of Ukraine’s territory, according to the latest issue of the Russia-Ukraine War Report Card.
kept.publisher: Russia Matters, Harvard Kennedy School Belfer Center
kept.relevance: The recent theater-wide territorial-change measure supplies background on the pace of Russian gains, with limited ability to describe localized infiltration into Ternuvate.

kept.excerpt: Videos published on February 22 show a Ukrainian servicemember operating in the northwestern part of Ternuvate. ISW experts found no visual evidence that Russian forces have held positions in Ternuvate since February 6, 2026.
kept.relevance: This dated report supplies settlement-specific historical evidence behind the question’s premise of a possible Russian re-entry, but is too old to establish July control.

kept.excerpt: Information about the alleged capture of the village of Ternuvate in the Zaporizhzhia region by Russian troops is not true; the settlement remains under the control of the Ukrainian Defense Forces. This was reported by the Operation Task Force "East" on Telegram and published in a video, according to Ukrinform.
kept.publisher: Ukrinform, citing Ukraine’s Operation Task Force East
kept.relevance: This contemporaneous Ukrainian military account documents the earlier dispute over Ternuvate’s control and underscores why capture claims require verification against the specified ISW layers.

search_notes: Frozen cutoff: 2026-07-18, inclusive. All retained sources display publication dates on or before the cutoff, verified through web_search results and indexed article text. Later-dated material, rolling pages without verifiable publication dates, and prediction-market or betting sources were excluded. web_fetch failed with a provider-configuration error; the requested fallback, agent-reach web read, returned RATE_LIMITED, so no full-page retrieval was available. Evidence is therefore limited to search-indexed text. No archived July 18 ISW map snapshot or consecutive finalized map-layer updates were verified, so these items do not establish settlement-boundary shading or satisfaction of the persistence rule. Market creation time was not supplied, and the provided resolution text ends mid-sentence. No forecast or resolution conclusion is included.
